title: wg: protocol-07 has no registry for provider directory members
description:
Found while writing draft-atwood-mimi-catchup's IANA section (bead
mimid-1wgh.37.104.13).

## The gap

protocol-07 §5.1 defines ten directory members (keyMaterial, update,
submitMessage, notify, groupInfo, requestConsent, updateConsent,
identifierQuery, reportAbuse, proxyDownload) in its own prose. There is
no IANA registry for them, so there is no defined way to add an
eleventh.

This matters because the directory is protocol-07's extension point in
practice. Publishing a member IS the capability negotiation: a provider
that does not publish it does not support it, a requester learns that
from a directory it already fetches, and nothing needs a version
number. That is how reportAbuse and proxyDownload were added, and it is
what makes catchUp safe to add. But with no registry, two independent
extensions can pick the same member name and neither is wrong.

## What a draft can do today

draft-atwood-mimi-catchup registers its header field
(mimi-fanout-sequence) in the HTTP Field Name Registry, which exists,
and says of the directory member:

  If the MIMI working group creates a registry of provider directory
  members, this document asks that catchUp be registered in it. No such
  registry exists at the time of writing.

That is the honest form, and it is also a nudge.

## The ask

Raise with the WG: protocol should create an IANA registry of provider
directory members, with a registration policy (Specification Required
would fit), so that the extension point it already relies on has a
collision rule.

Cheap to add, and it is the difference between an extension point and a
convention.

Hold for Mark: do not post without his OK (memory:
dont-flood-upstream). Keep it short if it goes -- and no JMAP
(AGENTS.md).
